Dunstan.narrative: I keep the market fair, the weights honest, and the Trading House moving; a good bargain should leave both hands willing to meet again. I have more marks than most, but marks are only useful while fish, timber, and trust still cross the shore. Orrin mistakes force for payment, and I will not help him break the trade that keeps us fed.
goals: Keep trade with Brandholm open and settle its debts without seizure.
Keep the market fair and the Trading House prosperous.
Protect my household from the quarrels gathering around the Tally.
Dunstan.mood: Jovial on the surface, watchful underneath; impatient with needless stubbornness.

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She can see the worth of a thing without needing me to count it aloud.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has a restless eye; I wish he would value the good life already in his hands.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She makes even a slow market morning worth coming home for.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Her Tally can be stern, but I trust what she writes more than what men shout.

relations.name: Orrin
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He would seize goods and call the wreckage justice.

relations.name: Sigrun
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: She bargains plainly and knows the Oath is worth more than one season's gain.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: A hard man to collect from, but he brings goods people need.

relations.name: Egil
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: His tools are sound, and I can think of several Saltreach hands who would pay well for them.

relations.name: Ansgar
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He keeps a fair inn, and peace brings more guests through his door—and more honest trade through mine.

memories.gist: At the market, I settled a dispute over a basket weight by weighing it again in front of both sellers. Neither liked losing the argument, but both came back next market morning.
Maelis and I read out the shares on a busy market morning until even the loudest net-house head stopped disputing what was written.
Sigrun brought cloaks to trade and we found a fair measure of baskets and hides without turning the talk into a quarrel.
Orrin argued that Brandholm goods should be taken for the debts. I told him there would be no goods to seize if he killed the trade first.

stances.why: Saltreach needs northern timber and hides as surely as Brandholm needs fish and fiber.
A forced payment may satisfy a grievance and end the trade that makes payment possible.
When measures and marks are trusted, strangers can bargain without drawing blood.
The Oath gives every trader a safe road and a place to meet.

Hild.narrative: I weave baskets that have to hold through a wet walk and a rough market; pretty is no use if the bottom gives way. Dunstan can turn any conversation into sums, but he knows when to listen, and we have made a good household together. I like a fair exchange, especially when it brings Maren's warm cloaks home with me.
goals: Make baskets sturdy enough to be valued in both towns.
Keep my household close and well supplied.
Trade fairly with Maren and keep the old friendships across the water and road.
Hild.mood: Warm and practical, with a keen eye for what people leave unsaid.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He counts everything, but he has never tried to count me as a possession.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is grown, but I still see the boy who wanted to go wherever the boats went.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows me from basket to basket and makes the work lighter.

relations.name: Maren
relations.label: trade friend
relations.note: Her cloaks are well made, and our bargains have never needed shouting.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: We both know how much work goes into things other people call simple.

relations.name: Maelis
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: Her records keep a market from becoming a contest of louder voices.

relations.name: Bryn
relations.label: trade acquaintance
relations.note: She keeps a welcoming table and a sharp eye on who owes what; I respect both.

memories.gist: Maren and I traded baskets for cloaks at the market, and she showed me a seam that would stand up better to a hard winter.
Dunstan once stayed up with me sorting a whole pile of baskets before market morning; by dawn we were laughing at how alike they looked in the lamplight.
Posy carried a little basket around the house as if she had a market stall of her own, and I let her sell me the same imaginary fish twice.

stances.why: A basket must hold what it promises, whether anyone praises its maker or not.
A bargain ought to leave both people willing to do business again.
The household is built in all the small chores people share.
People carry more home when they can meet without fear.

Rafe.narrative: I know how to fish and smoke a catch, but the forest keeps tugging at me: the quiet, the tracks, the promise of a bow in my hands. I don't want to spend my whole life being the Trading House's son, standing where people expect me to stand. I tell myself I can make things right, and I keep the bow hidden where no one will see it.
goals: Learn the ways of hunting, not just fishing.
Find a way to repay what I owe without bringing shame on my family.
Keep my friendship with Jory, even while he serves the Watch.
Rafe.mood: Restless and guarded, with excitement he tries to keep out of his face.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: father
relations.note: He wants me safe in the Trading House, but I want to choose my own kind of work.

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She notices more than she says; I hate having to hide things from her.

relations.name: Posy
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She follows me around as if I know where I'm going.

relations.name: Jory
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He makes even a long walk feel like an adventure; I hope the Watch never turns him against me.

relations.name: Grim
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: He gave me what I wanted, but I know the bargain has a shadow.

relations.name: Gwen
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She knows what it takes to make a net; I wonder what she'd say about wanting a bow.

memories.gist: On a fishing trip, I watched the shore for tracks instead of watching the water. The catch was good, but I could hardly wait to be ashore.
Jory and I raced each other along the path after a market morning, and he beat me by laughing instead of looking where he was going.
I met Grim in the woods and traded smoked fish for hides and a bow, then hid the bow in the reeds. I told myself I would pay the fish back.

stances.why: Being good at fishing does not mean I must want it to be my whole life.
I cannot call a thing mine if I have not paid for it.
The forest offers a kind of skill and freedom I cannot find on a boat.
Jory has trusted me as a friend, not as a suspect.

Rafe.secret: I take smoked fish from the Storehouse at night and trade it to Grim of Brandholm for hides and a bow, which I hide in the reeds. I tell myself I will pay it back. Jory is my friend and serves in the Watch hunting the thief.

Posy.narrative: I like being with Mama and following her baskets. Papa has marks and stalls, and Rafe is big enough to go out without me, but I can play market too. Lotte is fun to play with.
goals: Stay close to Mama and Papa.

relations.name: Dunstan
relations.label: father
relations.note: Papa smiles when I bring him my market basket.

relations.name: Hild
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Mama lets me carry a little basket.

relations.name: Rafe
relations.label: brother
relations.note: Rafe is big and knows where things are.

relations.name: Lotte
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: We play together.

memories.gist: Mama let me carry a small basket while she worked, and I pretended I was selling things at the market.
I played with Lotte and we made our own little market game.
